hints: Look at the sign of the enthalpy change and decide whether products should sit higher or lower than reactants.
Remember that $\Delta H^\ominus$ is the energy gap between reactants and products, here $+90$ kJ mol$^{-1}$ for $\frac{1}{2}\text{N}_2(g) + \frac{1}{2}\text{O}_2(g) \rightarrow \text{NO}(g)$.
Check where $E_a$ starts, it must be measured upward from the reactant energy to the top of the hump, not from the product level.
walkthrough:
**Decide endothermic or exothermic**

This reaction has $\Delta H^\ominus = +90$ kJ mol$^{-1}$. A positive sign means heat is taken in.

$$\frac{1}{2}\text{N}_2(g) + \frac{1}{2}\text{O}_2(g) \rightarrow \text{NO}(g) \quad \Delta H^\ominus > 0$$
So the product $\text{NO}(g)$ must be higher in energy than the reactants.

**Define what the two arrows must show**

$\Delta H^\ominus$ is products minus reactants. It goes from the reactant level up to the product level.

$$\Delta H^\ominus = H(\text{products}) - H(\text{reactants})$$
$E_a$ is transition state minus reactants. It goes from the reactant level up to the peak of the curve.

**Eliminate the exothermic diagram**

Diagram A puts $\text{NO}(g)$ below $\frac{1}{2}\text{N}_2(g) + \frac{1}{2}\text{O}_2(g)$. That is an exothermic profile with negative $\Delta H^\ominus$, so it cannot be right.

**Pick the diagram with both arrows correct**

Only the diagram with products above reactants, $\Delta H^\ominus$ from reactants up to products, and $E_a$ from reactants up to the peak matches both definitions. That is the correct pathway.

options.A: Shows NO(g) lower than reactants, an exothermic profile. This would mean negative $\Delta H^\ominus$, opposite to the given $+90$ kJ mol$^{-1}$. It confuses endothermic with exothermic.
options.B: Correctly puts NO(g) above reactants so $\Delta H^\ominus$ is positive, but $E_a$ is drawn from the product level up to the peak. $E_a$ must always start at the reactant energy, not the product energy.
options.C: Correctly puts NO(g) above $\frac{1}{2}N_2 + \frac{1}{2}O_2$ for an endothermic reaction. $\Delta H^\ominus$ goes from reactants up to products and $E_a$ goes from reactants up to the peak, matching both definitions.
options.D: Has the right energy levels and $\Delta H^\ominus$, but $E_a$ is drawn as a long downward arrow from the peak to reactants. $E_a$ is the energy barrier to climb from reactants, so it should be shown as an upward arrow starting at reactants. This presentation is not the accepted convention.
